To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SA solution is suitable for MIM.
the Sm(Co, Fe, Cu, Zr) 7.4 sintered magnet prepared by metal injection molding with the stearic acid solution has the best anti-oxidation effect.

(1) the antioxidation effect by silane solution is the best; (2) the antioxidation effects by SA solution and PMMA solution are not good enough, and (3) the antioxidation by silane solution severely damages the magnetic and microstructure of sintered magnets, while that by SA solution does not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the oxidation of Sm(Co,Cu,Fe,Zr)z sinnered magnets treated by MIM.
the effect of antioxidation treatment on the microstructure and magnetic properties of Sm(Co,Cu,Fe,Zr)z magnets by MIM.
the antioxidation effect and microstructure of the Sm(Co, Fe, Cu, Zr) sintered magnets prepared by MIM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MIM is a suitable method to prepare Sm(Co, Fe, Zrn)z sinter magnets.
SA is the most suitable antioxidant for Sm(Co, Fe, Cu, Zr) magnets by MIM.
the antioxidation of Sm(Co,Cu,Fe,Zr)z sentered magnets by MIP is better than that by MIM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MIM process is suitable for preparing high performance permanent magnets.
SA solution can be used to treat Sm(Co, Fe, Cu, Zr) z alloy powders in MIM.
the best antioxidation effect is achieved by SA solution and the best antioxidation method for MIM is SA solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the alloy powders treated with SA can prevent powders and magnets from oxidizing in a short time and the oxygen content of SmCo magnets is 3300mg*g 1 by MIM.
SA solution is the optimal method for preventing powders from oxidization in the MIM process.
SA solution is a suitable method for antioxidation in the MIM of Sm(Co,Cu,Fe,Zr)z sinnered magnets.
